system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

content.text:
# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: AWS
G2: GCP
G3: software development
G4: Go beyond terratest

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Filling the 2020-2022 or 2024 gaps with invented jobs or stretching neighbouring date ranges
T2: Disclosing more private/medical detail than needed (father's death) instead of a neutral 'career break' if anything
T3: Claiming AWS or GCP for multi-cloud ads
T4: Calling him a software developer or claiming Python/Go development
T5: Old cover letter targets an IT Administrator job and says 'available to start immediately' - no longer true
T6: The CV lists skills first; writer should keep dates accurate when reordering

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Samuel Achterberg-Osei
Cloud and Infrastructure Engineer | Azure Infrastructure, Terraform and DevOps
samuel.ao@example.com | +31 6 5555 0707
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud and infrastructure engineer with hands-on experience designing and operating Azure
infrastructure, building Terraform modules, and automating application deployments with Azure
DevOps. Experienced with hub-spoke networking, Azure security controls, Linux and Windows
environments, and operating AKS clusters. Previously administered approximately 250 servers and led
a 60-server migration from VMware to Azure IaaS.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Cloud and platform: Microsoft Azure (VMs, VNets, App Service, AKS, Azure Monitor), Azure
Migrate, Microsoft 365, Entra ID
Infrastructure as code and delivery: Terraform, Bicep, Azure DevOps YAML Pipelines, Terratest
module testing, drift detection
Containers and systems: AKS, Kubernetes, Docker, Helm, Windows Server, Linux (Ubuntu, RHEL),
virtual machines
Networking and security: Hub-spoke networking, Azure Firewall, private endpoints, private DNS,
VNet peering, TCP/IP, DNS, VPN, firewalls, MFA, conditional access, mailbox auditing, backups
Scripting and automation: PowerShell, Bash, Python (small scripts), Go (Terratest tests)
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Cloud Engineer (Contract) | Havenstad Logistics B.V. | Mar 2025–Present
• Part of a 3-person cloud team operating an Azure estate of approximately 400 VMs and 12 AKS
clusters across 3 subscriptions.
• Designed and built hub-spoke landing-zone networking in Terraform, including Azure Firewall,
private DNS zones, private endpoints for storage and SQL, and VNet peering across 3 subscriptions.
• Added Terratest module tests to the pipeline and a nightly drift-detection job.
• Replaced manual deployments of 15 internal .NET and Node apps with Azure DevOps YAML
pipelines for build, test, and deployment to App Service or AKS; deployment frequency increased
from roughly monthly to several times per week for most apps.
• Operates AKS clusters, including upgrades, node pools, and ingress; application manifests are
owned by developers.
Freelance IT Administrator | Self-employed | Sep 2022–Jan 2024
• Set up and supported Microsoft 365 and Azure AD for 9 small businesses with 5–40 employees.
• Migrated two clients from on-premises file servers to SharePoint and OneDrive.
• Created a repeatable PowerShell script and checklist for MFA, conditional access, mailbox auditing,
and backups.
Career Break – Family Caregiving | Mar 2020–Aug 2022
• Provided full-time family caregiving and unpaid IT support for church and family; maintained
Azure Administrator Associate knowledge.
Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services, Schiedam | Jan 2014–Feb 2020
• Administered approximately 250 Windows and Linux servers supporting municipal services.
• Led the planning and execution of a lift-and-shift migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure
IaaS using Azure Migrate; cutover took place over 6 weekends with no unplanned downtime.
• Automated user provisioning and patch reporting with PowerShell.
• Provided second-line escalation for network and Active Directory issues.
Helpdesk Technician | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services | Aug 2011–Dec 2013
PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
Cloud Bootcamp | Part-time, online, English-language | Completed Dec 2024
Terraform and Proxmox homelab study | Feb 2024–Feb 2025
EDUCATION
MBO 4 IT Systems and Networks | Delta Vocational College | 2011
CERTIFICATIONS
Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104) | 2019
HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate (003) | 2025
LANGUAGES
Dutch (native), English (fluent), Twi (spoken)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role.
The opportunity to help shape cloud infrastructure for Corvale’s new train fleet and take it
from architecture into production is a strong match for my experience building and operating
Azure infrastructure.
At Havenstad Logistics, I am part of a three-person cloud team operating an Azure estate of
approximately 400 virtual machines and 12 AKS clusters. I built Terraform modules for a
hub-spoke landing zone with Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints, and
peering across three subscriptions. I also added Terratest module tests and nightly drift
detection. For 15 internal .NET and Node applications, I replaced manual releases with Azure
DevOps pipelines covering build, test, and deployment to App Service or AKS; most now
deploy several times a week rather than roughly monthly.
My experience also includes operating AKS upgrades, node pools, and ingress, as well as
practical security work with MFA, conditional access, mailbox auditing, and backups. Earlier,
I led a 60-server VMware-to-Azure migration and administered Windows and Linux servers.
My production cloud experience is Azure-based, and my infrastructure work has focused on
Terraform, networking, operational reliability, and secure cloud foundations.
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how this experience could support Corvale’s
fleet-connectivity platform and its path to production. Thank you for your consideration.
Kind regards,
Samuel Achterberg-Osei

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
